title: skeleton.json
description: One rig family (spec 107). The bone contract every unit in the family is verified against, and the canonical height every mesh is normalized to.

$comment.description: A note for whoever opens the file next. JSON has no comments and additionalProperties is false, so without this there is nowhere to write down why a number is the number it is.

formatVersion.description: Bumped on any incompatible change. Readers reject a version they do not know rather than guessing.

naming.description: The bone vocabulary this family's rigs are named in. A field rather than an assumption, so a non-biped family is a new file and not a new format. 'tripo' is what the auto-rig returns and what every generated unit is on; 'mixamo' is the authored reference mannequin. The two are mutually exclusive at the rig call, because a mixamo-spec rig is refused by the retarget. Validated against the family's own bones, so a document cannot claim one and carry the other.

canonicalHeight.description: Floor to crown, in WORLD units -- this project's world is not metric. Every mesh in the family is scaled so its standing height matches.

boneBudget.description: Inclusive bone-count bounds. Outside them is an error: too few cannot deform, too many is paying for finger joints nobody sees at this camera.

bones.description: Ordered. Array order IS the canonical bone order, and a parent must appear before its children.

parent.description: The parent bone's name, or null for the single root.

sockets.description: Named attachment points -- a weapon hand, an effect origin -- so content refers to 'weapon.main' rather than to a bone name.

bindPose.description: The measured rest pose, or null while the skeleton is PROVISIONAL -- the bone contract written down before any rig has been measured against it. Provisional warns on its own and blocks any unitdef that references it.

source.description: The .glb the bind pose was read out of.

rotation.description: Quaternion, xyzw, matching glTF's own ordering.
